2. The relevant facts, for the disposal of this petition, are that the petitioners and preform respondent No. 25 instituted Title Suit No. 85 of 1991 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Narayangonj, which was subsequently transferred in the Additional Court of Joint District Judge, Narayangonj and renumbered as Title Suit No. 168 of 1992, for declaration of their title in the suit land stating, inter alia, that one Bangu Sheikh had raiyati interest in 03.13 acres of land described in the schedule of the plaint. His daughter Payron Nessa and her husband Golam Hossain used to live in his house. Their son Kalimuddin was given in marriage with Aushi Bibi. Bangu Sheikh transferred 1.94 acres of land from different plots to Aushi Bibi by way of Heba and delivered possession. He also transferred .64 and .55 acre of land from Plot No.33 and 110 respectively to his daughter Payron Nessa and wife Rupjan Bibi. Those .64 and .55 acres of land were recorded in the names of Payron Nessa and Rupjan Bibi Similarly. 1.94 acres of land was recorded in the name of Aushi Bibi in C.S. Khatian. Rupjan Bibi died-leaving her daughter Payron Nessa and thereafter Payron Nessa died leaving his son Kalimuddin who became owner of 1.19 acres of land of Plot No. 64 and 110. Kalimuddin died leaving his son Abdul Manaf and wife Aushi Bibi. Abdul Manaf died leaving his mother Aushi Bibi wife Rabban Bibi, sons Yasin and Abul Hossain and daughters Mehar Negar, Suraiya Begum, Tunu Bibi and Gul Akhter. Then, Aushi Bibi died leaving her aforesaid sons and daughter. The plaintiffs and proforma defendants arc successive heirs of said Kalimuddin and Aushi Bibi. The principal defendant Nos. 1-4 had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. In S.A. Operation, the suit land was erroneously recorded in the name of Aushi Miah. Taking Opportunity of such erroneous record of right the defendant Nos. 1-4 claimed title in the suit land. Hence was the suit. 

 6. This Division earlier affirmed the findings of the High Court Division that C.S. record of right was prepared in the name of Aushi and thereafter S.A and R.S. Khatian were also prepared in the name of Aushi Miah. The High Court Division considering Heba deed (Ext. F). sale deed (Ext. G and G-1), Rent receipts (Ext. E series), and three records of right reversed the concurrent the findings of the Courts of facts. Mr. Abdus Salam Khan failed to show any error apparent on the face of the record or any new and important matter which had not been considered by this Division at the time of adjudication of the Civil Petition or any other sufficient cause to review the judgment.
